For all $\kappa ,\epsilon >0$ there is $\rho (\kappa ,\epsilon )$ such that, if $\eta $ is minimizing with endpoints $y_1,y_2$, $z'\in \eta $ is nearest to $z$, and $R(z')d(z',y_i)^2>\rho $, then $z,z'$ are $\epsilon $-neck centers and \[ \max \{ R(z)d(z,z')^2,R(z')d(z,z')^2\} <4\pi ^2. \]
Proof

\sketch Apply the proposition at $z'$ with a smaller neck parameter; the orthogonal segment $zz'$ lies near a spherical cross-section.

\label{longsegment}
For all $\kappa,\epsilon>0$ there is $\rho(\kappa,\epsilon)$ such that, if
$\eta$ is minimizing with endpoints $y_1,y_2$, $z'\in\eta$ is nearest to $z$,
and $R(z')d(z',y_i)^2>\rho$, then $z,z'$ are $\epsilon$-neck centers and
\[
\max\{R(z)d(z,z')^2,R(z')d(z,z')^2\}<4\pi^2.
\]
\end{corollary}
